narrative.overview:
Field service runs on paper: the work order, the day sheet, the estimate pad. Zaxvio is the digital version of that paper, and the system keeps its manners. Surfaces are warm off-white paper. Text is near-black carbon ink. Times, money and counts are typed figures that line up in columns. One Safety Orange mark shows what to do next or where you are, the way a marker circles the job that matters on a printed sheet. On the landing page the ruling is literal: hairlines every 3rem behind the headline and the closing band, and a time-ruled day sheet as the hero. Inside the app the same idea shows up as order: bordered cards, one-row toolbars, mono figures and pill-shaped status.

The density is a working tool's, not a brochure's. Body text is 14px, and toolbars, filter tabs and table rows are compact so a day's worth of jobs fits on one screen. Expression lives in the details: the orange hairline across the top of the navbar, the orange glow when you pick up a job card, a status pill's colour. Dark mode is a full peer, not an inversion: the warm neutral ladder is restepped so every surface still rises in the right order.

Rejected on purpose, and recorded in the code where each was removed: "AI startup" gloss (purple-on-white gradients, aurora or nebula backdrops, glow used as decoration), device mockups around the product, spinners, and cool blue-slate greys or generic system fonts.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper neutrals (hue 25–32, low saturation) that rise in four tonal steps.
One accent, Safety Orange, used for action, location and the current hour.
Three faces with fixed jobs: Space Grotesk for headings and labels, DM Sans for prose and controls, DM Mono for anything read as data.
Hairline borders and gentle corners. Pills mean state, rectangles mean containers and actions.
Motion that explains a change and then stops. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the movement goes and the fade stays.

rules.name: The Motion Explains a Change Rule
rules.body: Things animate when they appear, move or change state, then stop. A resting screen is still. Nothing animates while it's being dragged or panned, and every keyframe has a `prefers-reduced-motion` override. The only continuous motions allowed are signals: the emergency-priority pulse, the empty automation canvas's slow breath, the help assistant's typing dots while a reply is pending, and the impersonation bar's live dot. Each of the last two stops for reduced motion.

rules.name: The Validated Data Colour Rule
rules.body: Data colours come from `lib/constants/chart-palette.ts`, which reads only tokens: categorical slots in fixed order and never cycled (past the fifth, a bucket folds into a neutral "Other"), status for good or bad, overdue for age. A single series is one hue, not a colour per bar. No hex in a chart: a colour that is not a token is a colour nobody validated.

rules.name: The One Mark Rule
rules.body: Safety Orange is the only accent. It marks the next action, the current place, or now. If a screen has orange in more than a handful of places, one of them is lying.

rules.name: The Rising Sheet Rule
rules.body: Surfaces must rise in this order in both themes: background ≤ surface < second sheet < card. In dark mode borders stay lighter than cards (19% against 13%), or the borders vanish. Any neutral change has to keep this order.

rules.name: The Same-Hue Rule
rules.body: Neutrals stay on the orange's side of the colour wheel (hue 25–32, under 25% saturation). A cool grey makes the orange read as an intrusion instead of an accent.

rules.name: The Fill, Not the Text Rule
rules.body: Safety Orange is a fill. On it, labels are Carbon Ink (`--brand-foreground`/`--primary-foreground`): 5.8:1 in light and 6.2:1 in dark, where white was 2.85:1 and 2.68:1. When orange has to be read, it is Orange Deep through `text-brand-ink`, never `text-brand` (2.7:1 on light surfaces). "Read" means words and numbers, the focus ring, and any icon that carries meaning on its own: a selection check, an icon-only button, a toggled toolbar icon, a scroll hint (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of those). Bright `text-brand` is kept for exactly three things: a decorative glyph beside a heading that names the same thing (section-header, empty-state and activity-type icons, icon tiles), the logotype, and orange on the always-dark Night Shift slab, where Orange Deep would fail instead. In dark mode `--brand-ink` is Safety Orange, so the split only shows in light mode. Fixed in the tokens and swept through the product on 2026-10-16 (landing audit LAND-03/06).

rules.name: The Figures Rule
rules.body: Anything read as a number (a time, an amount, a count, a job number) is set in DM Mono with tabular figures (the `.tnum` utility), so columns line up and values don't jitter as they change.

rules.name: The Three Faces Rule
rules.body: Space Grotesk, DM Sans and DM Mono, each with its own job. There is no fourth face, and Inter, Roboto, Arial or system defaults are never used.

rules.name: The One Row Rule
rules.body: A list's filter tabs, search and extra controls share one header row: tabs on the left, everything else pushed right. Never two stacked toolbars.

rules.name: The Tonal-First Rule
rules.body: Separate things with the surface ladder and a hairline before reaching for a shadow. A shadow at rest never goes above "resting card".

rules.name: The Grab Glow Rule
rules.body: The orange glow means "you can pick this up". It belongs on draggable or grabbable objects (job cards), never on static cards for decoration.

rules.name: The Pill Means State Rule
rules.body: Full-round shapes carry state, filters, counts and people. Containers and actions are gently cornered rectangles. A pill-shaped container or a square status tag breaks the reading.

dos: Do take every colour from the tokens (`bg-card`, `text-ink`, `border-border`, `bg-brand`) so both themes stay correct. Status colours always get an explicit `dark:` pair.
Do keep Safety Orange to action, location and now (The One Mark Rule).
Do set times, money and counts in DM Mono with tabular figures (The Figures Rule).
Do keep the surface ladder rising in both themes when touching any neutral (The Rising Sheet Rule).
Do use the Night Shift slab for customer-facing portals and the auth shell, and keep printed quotes ink-on-white with no dark band and no buttons.
Do use skeletons shaped like the content for every loading state.
Do use the motion vocabulary's curve and durations, and attach new arrivals to a shell or a shared primitive rather than to one page.
Do give every animation a `prefers-reduced-motion` override, and stop motion while the user drags or pans.

Do write orange text and meaningful orange icons with `text-brand-ink`, put Carbon Ink labels on orange fills, and keep bright `text-brand` for decorative glyphs beside a heading, the logo and the Night Shift slab (The Fill, Not the Text Rule).
donts: Don't use "AI startup" gloss: no purple-on-white gradients, aurora or nebula backdrops, or glow as decoration.
Don't put the product in a laptop or phone frame. Show the real object, like the day sheet.

Don't use spinners (`animate-spin`, `Loader2`) for loading, or for "working". A busy control changes its label and disables itself, and a wait on a person shows an hourglass. The last six spinners were removed on 2026-10-16.
Don't loop anything that isn't a signal. A hint nudges twice and rests, and an attention cue pulses three times and rests.
Don't use cool blue-slate neutrals or raw `gray-*` classes, and never Inter, Roboto, Arial or system defaults.
Don't add a second accent colour. Teal, indigo and the chart hues are data identity, not UI chrome.
Don't put the orange grab glow on anything that can't be picked up.
Don't stack two toolbars on a list page (The One Row Rule).
Don't put white text on Safety Orange, or use `text-brand` for anything that has to be read (LAND-03, LAND-06).
